children: PayPal Holdings, Inc.

’s PYPL expanding integration strategy is giving its engagement story a broader reach. The company is bringing PayPal and Venmo into more everyday payment occasions, including college tuition, retail purchases and consumer financing. New integrations with Illumia, Nelnet Campus Commerce and TouchNet are extending the platforms into education payments, while integrations and platform initiatives across Buy Now, Pay Later (“BNPL”) and merchant services are further widening distribution.
The market has already rewarded that progress. PYPL has outperformed key rivals such as
Visa Inc.
V and
Mastercard Incorporated
MA over the past six months, reflecting investor confidence in PayPal’s growth.
Even so, the stock has pulled back from its six-month highs in August 2026, keeping the debate open over whether the current valuation still leaves enough room for further gains.

The bigger question is whether broader distribution can translate into deeper customer and merchant relationships rather than simply higher transaction volume. More payment use cases, wider BNPL availability and an increasingly connected merchant platform could strengthen engagement and monetization over time if PayPal can sustain execution and turn its expanding network into durable growth.
PayPal & Venmo Bring More Payment Choice to College Tuition

PayPal Holdings is broadening the role of PayPal and Venmo beyond online checkout by embedding its payment tools into more everyday financial experiences. Its recent integration push spans education, retail, consumer finance and merchant services, supporting efforts to deepen engagement, widen distribution and create more ways for customers to use its network.

A key development is PayPal and Venmo’s expansion into tuition payments through new integrations with Illumia, Nelnet Campus Commerce and TouchNet. Students and families at participating schools can now pay tuition fees through existing campus payment portals using PayPal or Venmo. The integrations are live at institutions including Butler University, Kansas State University, Michigan State University and Texas Tech University, with more schools expected to join in 2026.

The tuition initiative extends PayPal’s growing college presence. The company had already built momentum through agreements with the Big Ten and Big 12, Venmo NIL partnerships, college-branded cards and student ambassadors. Bringing tuition into the ecosystem gives PayPal exposure to a major payment category while offering users familiar funding choices, including bank accounts, cards and PayPal or Venmo balances.
Integration-Led Growth Supports PayPal’s Late-2026 Momentum

PayPal is also widening distribution for BNPL. In the second quarter of 2026, Temu introduced PayPal BNPL in Canada, expanding availability to eight markets globally, while Home Depot Canada added upstream presentment of PayPal’s BNPL options. These integrations can raise product visibility earlier in the shopping journey and help PayPal capture more checkout volume.

On the merchant side, PayPal is working to unify Braintree, PayPal Complete Payments and Hyperwallet into a single foundation. Management expects these efforts to improve interoperability and expand self-processing capabilities, merchant lending and payouts. Over time, the unified platform is expected to provide greater flexibility and reach while supporting emerging use cases such as PYUSD-enabled commerce and agentic payments.

These initiatives come amid improving momentum across PayPal’s business. Second-quarter total payment volume (TPV) rose 10% to $486.4 billion, while Venmo and Braintree continued to deliver mid-teens TPV growth. Broader integrations, financial-services expansion and ongoing technology upgrades are likely to help PayPal finish 2026 with a more diversified growth profile while strengthening customer and merchant engagement heading into 2027.
PayPal’s Key Risks

PayPal faces intense competition across checkout, BNPL and digital payments. At the same time, its broad technology modernization and platform-integration efforts create execution risk. Delays, weaker partner adoption or higher-than-expected costs could slow growth, pressure margins and reduce returns from these initiatives overall.
PYPL Shares Trade at a Discount

PayPal shares are trading cheap, as suggested by the Value Score of A. In terms of forward 12-month Price/Earnings (P/E), PYPL stock is trading at 9.39X compared with the Zacks Financial Transaction Services industry’s 17.58X.
PYPL’s Earnings Estimate Revision Trends Upward

PayPal’s estimate revisions reflect a favorable trend for full-year 2026. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for 2026 EPS has moved a cent upward to $5.38 over the past month. This implies a 1.3% rise year over year.
What Should Investors Do With PYPL Now?

PayPal’s expanding integrations, improving engagement across Venmo and BNPL, platform modernization and solid TPV growth strengthen its long-term growth prospects. Favorable earnings estimate revisions and a discounted valuation also support the investment case.

However, execution risks, competitive pressure and the stock’s recent pullback warrant some caution despite improving fundamentals. Investors may prefer to see more consistent evidence that broader distribution is translating into sustainable earnings growth. Therefore, investors may prefer to wait before adding this stock to their portfolio, while those who already have own it may consider holding their positions.
